title: Tool execution and dependency installs run synchronously inside async handlers, freezing the whole server
failure_scenario: api_run_tool (main.py:182) and mcp_endpoint -> MCPHandler.call_tool (mcp_server.py:141) are `async def` but call run_tool(), which does blocking subprocess.run() (up to OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS + 15 s, i.e. 45 s by default), a blocking pip/npm install (up to 120 s) and a busy-wait lock loop with time.sleep(0.1) (up to 125 s), all on the single uvicorn event loop. While one LLM client calls a slow tool, every other request is stalled: the dashboard, /api/config, other MCP clients' tools/list and tools/call, and any reverse-proxy health check. A first-run install plus a slow script can freeze the service for more than 4 minutes, and LLM clients time out and retry, piling up more blocking calls.
evidence: Verified on the isolated instance. While a 5 s tool (time.sleep(5)) ran via POST /api/tools/t_sleep/run, a concurrent GET /api/config took 4.51 s. During a real first-run `requests` install (1.24 s total), a concurrent GET /api/config took 0.94 s, i.e. it waited for the install to finish. The README only acknowledges that dependency preparation may block; script execution blocking is not documented.
suggested_fix: Run run_tool off the event loop: declare the handlers as plain `def` so FastAPI uses its threadpool, or `await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(run_tool, tool, arguments)`, or use asyncio.create_subprocess_exec. Add a concurrency limit (semaphore) per tool and overall, and run installs in a worker thread with the existing file lock.

title: Non-UTF-8 script output discards the real stdout and exit code
failure_scenario: subprocess.run(..., text=True) decodes with strict errors. If a script prints any byte sequence that isn't valid UTF-8 (a Latin-1/CP1252 file's contents, binary data, a truncated multibyte character), UnicodeDecodeError is raised inside subprocess.run and caught by the generic `except Exception` (runner.py:96). The result then has stdout='' and exit_code=1, and stderr carries the codec message instead of the script's real stderr. The tool's actual output and its real exit status are lost.
evidence: Verified. A script that writes b'result ok \xff\n' and exits 3 returned {"stdout":"","stderr":"'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 10: invalid start byte","exit_code":1}.
suggested_fix: Pass encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' (or capture bytes and decode with errors='replace'/'backslashreplace') so the output and returncode are preserved; report the decoding issue as a note rather than replacing the result.

title: Successful MCP results append stderr to stdout, corrupting JSON output
failure_scenario: call_tool always appends `[stderr] ...` to the single text content item, even when the tool succeeds (isError=false). The documented contract is to print JSON to stdout, but any library warning on stderr makes the result unparseable for clients and LLM post-processing. Examples include DeprecationWarning, urllib3 NotOpenSSLWarning, and the npm/pip notices the live test already works around. Warnings are not failures, but the response mixes them into the payload.
evidence: Verified. A tool that prints {"ok": true} and writes 'DeprecationWarning: something' to stderr returned text '{"ok": true}\n[stderr] DeprecationWarning: something' with isError=false, and json.loads(text) fails. tests/test_live_examples.py already splits on '\n[stderr] ' to work around this.
suggested_fix: On success, return stdout as the only text item, or put stderr in a separate content item / _meta field. Only fold stderr into the text when isError is true. Consider structuredContent when stdout is valid JSON.

title: JSON-RPC notifications get an error response (notifications/initialized -> -32601 with id null)
failure_scenario: Every MCP client sends `notifications/initialized` (no id) right after initialize, and may send notifications/cancelled. _handle_rpc treats any unknown method, including notifications, as a request and returns HTTP 200 with {"id":null,"error":{"code":-32601}}. JSON-RPC 2.0 forbids replying to notifications, and MCP Streamable HTTP requires 202 Accepted with no body. Strict clients (e.g. the TypeScript SDK transport) receive an unsolicited response with id null and raise transport errors or abort the session handshake.
evidence: Verified. POST /mcp {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"} returned HTTP 200 '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found: notifications/initialized"}}'.
suggested_fix: If the message has no "id" member, process it (or ignore unknown notifications) and return Response(status_code=202) with an empty body. Explicitly accept notifications/initialized and notifications/cancelled.

title: Tools saved by earlier versions with non-object schemas become unrunnable and unsaveable, with no migration
failure_scenario: Up to commit 42a5dd1, ToolIn.json_schema accepted any dict (e.g. {"properties":{...}} without "type":"object", or remote $refs) and stored it verbatim. The current code still advertises that stored schema in tools/list, but validate_schema() rejects it at call time. MCP tools/call, dashboard Run / Test and dashboard Save all fail. The dashboard save always carries the stored schema, and the UI has no schema editor, so the user can't repair the tool from the product at all. Only a hand-crafted API PUT can fix it.
evidence: Verified by inserting a row shaped like a 42a5dd1 save (json_schema_json='{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}}'). tools/list advertised inputSchema {'properties': {'x': {'type': 'string'}}}. MCP tools/call returned isError 'inputSchema must declare type object'. POST /run returned 422 with the same message. A dashboard-shaped PUT (code edit, schema carried over) returned 422 'Value error, inputSchema must declare type object'.
suggested_fix: Add a startup or on-read normalisation that repairs or flags legacy schemas (e.g. wrap in {type: object} when the top level has properties, otherwise fall back to EMPTY_SCHEMA with a visible warning). Make tools/list skip or repair invalid schemas. Let the dashboard save with an explicit 'reset schema' option.

title: Legacy duplicate-name rows are advertised twice in tools/list and can't be deleted from the dashboard
failure_scenario: Commit 42a5dd1's POST /api/tools created a new id on every call with no duplicate check, so a double-click Save or a repeated example install left two rows with the same name. The README says such rows are preserved. MCPHandler.tools() doesn't de-duplicate, so tools/list returns the same tool name twice. LLM APIs reject tool lists with duplicate names (e.g. Anthropic and OpenAI require unique tool/function names), so every chat that loads this MCP server fails. Calls always hit the first row, leaving the other unreachable. The dashboard can't fix it: Database.delete with If-Match requires exactly one row (database.py:190), so deleting either copy returns 412 'Tool changed in another tab' forever.
evidence: Verified. Inserted a second 'dup_tool' row: tools/list contained 'dup_tool' 2 times. DELETE /api/tools/dup_tool with If-Match set to each row's revision returned HTTP 412 for both rows. MCP and dashboard runs both executed the first row ('first').
suggested_fix: De-duplicate in MCPHandler.tools() (keep the newest row and log a warning). Allow conditional delete/update by id (match If-Match against any row with that name and delete that id). Add a startup report or an admin action to resolve duplicates. Consider a UNIQUE index once duplicates are resolved.

title: All tools share one cwd that is also sys.path[0], and scratch files are never cleaned up
failure_scenario: Every tool's code is written to SCRATCH_ROOT/<id>.py and runs with cwd=SCRATCH_ROOT. Python puts the script's directory first on sys.path. Any file a tool writes with a relative path lands in a directory shared by every tool, so tools clobber each other's output.json/data.csv. A file one tool writes (e.g. helpers.py, or one named like a stdlib or PyPI module such as json.py or requests.py) is imported by every other Python tool, silently changing their behaviour or breaking all of them. Code files are never removed, so deleted tools' source stays on disk indefinitely. With more than one worker, two runs of the same tool rewrite the same <id>.py.
evidence: Verified. A tool reported cwd and sys.path[0] both as <run>/tmp, with the other tools' .py files visible. writer_tool created of_shared_probe.py in its cwd, and reader_tool then successfully imported it ({"imported_from_other_tool": "defined by writer_tool"}). After DELETE /api/tools/t_slow, its <id>.py was still present (10 files accumulated). The README documents a 'shared scratch directory' but not import shadowing or the lack of cleanup.
suggested_fix: Create a per-run tempfile.TemporaryDirectory under SCRATCH_ROOT, write the script there, use it as cwd, and remove it afterwards. Run Python with -P (3.11+) or -I-equivalent flags so the script directory isn't prepended to sys.path. Delete scratch copies when a tool is deleted.

title: A child process holding stdout turns a successful run into a 'timeout' and survives the kill
failure_scenario: subprocess.run waits for EOF on the stdout/stderr pipes, not only for the script to exit. If a script starts any background child that inherits the pipes (a helper daemon, a library worker, `subprocess.Popen` without redirection), the script's own successful exit is ignored. The call blocks until timeout+15 s (and, per BE-01, freezes the server), is reported as exit 124 / timed_out with stdout discarded, and only the direct child is killed. The grandchild keeps running, so repeated calls accumulate orphans.
evidence: Verified with OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS=2000. A script that ran subprocess.Popen(['sleep','37']), printed a line and exited immediately returned after 17.02 s: {"stdout":"","stderr":"Script exceeded 2000ms timeout","exit_code":124,"timed_out":true}. `pgrep` showed `sleep 37` still running after the response; it was cleaned up manually.
suggested_fix: Start scripts with start_new_session=True and on timeout os.killpg() the whole process group. After the main process exits, stop reading after a short grace period and kill the remaining group members. Consider running under a cgroup or prlimit.

title: Unbounded stdout/stderr capture is held in memory and returned in full
failure_scenario: capture_output=True buffers everything the script prints for up to 45 s, then the full text is returned in the HTTP JSON response and in the MCP text content. A runaway print loop, or a tool that dumps a large file, can exhaust the container's memory (killing the service for all clients) or push megabytes into an LLM client's context window, causing client failures.
evidence: Verified. A tool that writes 20,000,000 bytes to stdout produced a 20,000,075-byte HTTP response in 0.21 s with no truncation or warning.
suggested_fix: Stream the pipes into bounded buffers (e.g. keep the first and last N KB, OMNIFORGE_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES), mark the result as truncated, and kill the process group when the cap is exceeded.

title: Scripts inherit the full application environment, including OMNIFORGE_API_KEY
failure_scenario: environment = os.environ.copy() passes OMNIFORGE_API_KEY (the only credential protecting POST /mcp) and any other container secrets to every tool and to the code of every package it installs. A debugging tool that prints os.environ, or a compromised dependency, puts the key into tool output. That output then flows to the LLM client, chat transcripts and logs, and the key grants MCP access from anywhere on the LAN. The installer already uses a minimal environment, so the runner is inconsistent with it.
evidence: Verified (boolean only, value never printed). A tool returned {"api_key_var_present": true}. tests/test_dependencies.py asserts runtime_env['OMNIFORGE_API_KEY'] == 'sentinel', so the behaviour is locked in by tests.
suggested_fix: Build an allowlisted environment for scripts (PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR, PYTHONPATH/NODE_PATH plus an explicit per-tool allowlist), mirroring _installer_environment(). Update the test to assert the key is absent.

title: Cross-site request forgery: any web page can run or toggle tools through a LAN user's browser
failure_scenario: POST /api/tools/{name}/run accepts an empty body, and POST /api/tools/{name}/toggle takes no body. Neither checks Origin, Host or Content-Type, so both are CORS 'simple requests' that browsers send cross-origin without a preflight. If anyone on the trusted LAN opens a malicious or compromised site, it can blind-fire fetch('http://<omniforge>:8000/api/tools/<name>/run',{method:'POST',mode:'no-cors'}) against guessable names (e.g. the four dashboard example names). That executes those tools with {} or disables them. Because there's no Host check, DNS rebinding could escalate this to full read/write API access and arbitrary tool creation; this was not verified.
evidence: Verified. A POST with Origin: http://example.invalid, Content-Type: text/plain and an empty body to /api/tools/t_echo/run returned 200 {"stdout":"executed"}. The same request to /toggle returned 200 {"is_active":false}.
suggested_fix: On all mutating endpoints, require Content-Type: application/json and a custom header (e.g. X-OmniForge: 1), reject requests whose Origin/Referer doesn't match the Host, and validate Host against an allowlist (TrustedHostMiddleware) to block DNS rebinding.

title: A script exiting with code 124 is reported as a timeout
failure_scenario: timed_out is derived from exit_code == 124 rather than from the TimeoutExpired branch. Any script that exits 124 is reported as timed_out=true, and MCP appends '[timeout]'. That includes scripts wrapping a command with GNU `timeout`, which itself exits 124, and scripts using 124 as an application error code. Users chase a non-existent server timeout.
evidence: Verified. sys.exit(124) after printing returned timed_out=true in 11 ms, and MCP text 'normal failure\n[exit 124]\n[timeout]'.
suggested_fix: Set a timed_out boolean in the `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` branch and use it, independent of the exit code.

title: Timeout fires 15 s after the configured value, and partial output is discarded
failure_scenario: The effective timeout is OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS + 15 s, but the error message reports only the configured value. An operator who sets 2000 ms to protect the single event loop still gets 17 s stalls. On timeout, stdout is replaced with '' although TimeoutExpired.stdout carries what was printed so far, so progress output useful for diagnosing a hang is lost.
evidence: Verified with OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS=2000. A 5 s script completed normally (exit 0, 5013 ms). A 30 s script that printed 'partial progress' (flushed) was killed at 17.02 s with stdout '' and stderr 'Script exceeded 2000ms timeout'. The +15 s is documented in the README.
suggested_fix: Use the configured value (optionally plus a small grace period that the message states). Keep exc.stdout/exc.stderr (decoded leniently) in the result.

title: A crash during install leaves .install-* staging trees that are never cleaned up
failure_scenario: The `finally: shutil.rmtree(staging)` doesn't run if the process is killed (container restart, OOM, deploy) during pip/npm install. The partially populated .install-XXXX directory stays in the persistent omniforge_lib volume forever. Later successful installs create a new staging directory and never sweep old ones, so repeated restarts during installs steadily leak disk on the NAS volume.
evidence: Verified. SIGKILL of the server during a real `requests==2.32.3` install left lib/<hash>/python3/.install-ddvjvdpj. After restart the rerun installed successfully (exit 0), and the orphaned staging directory was still present.
suggested_fix: While holding the per-digest lock, remove stale `.install-*` siblings older than INSTALL_TIMEOUT (they can only belong to dead installers because the lock is held), or sweep on startup.

title: Hardcoded installer PATH means npm isn't found outside the Docker image layout
failure_scenario: _installer_environment fixes PATH to /opt/venv/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin and looks npm up only there. If Node is installed anywhere else (nvm, /opt/node, a future image change or a dev machine), every Node tool with requirements fails with 'npm runtime is unavailable' even though the runner found node. npm's `#!/usr/bin/env node` can also resolve a different node than the one that runs the script.
evidence: Verified. In WSL (node in ~/of-env/node/bin), 2 unit tests error with DependencyError('npm runtime is unavailable'): test_cache_hash_tool_language_and_order and test_minimal_environment_official_installer_flags_and_runtime_environment. They pass only inside the image.
suggested_fix: Derive npm from the resolved node runtime (Path(node).parent / 'npm') and prepend that directory to the installer PATH. Mock npm discovery in unit tests.

title: Requirement validation accepts archive filenames and rejects canonical .postN/.devN pins
failure_scenario: The README says tarballs are rejected, but the name regexes accept 'foo.tar.gz', 'foo.zip', 'foo.whl' (Python) and 'foo.tgz', 'foo.tar.gz' (Node). pip and npm treat these as local archive paths rather than registry package names, so the requirement silently means something other than what validation intends (it currently resolves inside the fresh staging directory and fails with a confusing error). Conversely, the PEP 440 canonical pins 'pkg==1.0.post1' and 'pkg==1.0.dev1' are rejected while the non-canonical '1.0post1' is accepted.
evidence: Verified by calling validate_requirements(). ACCEPT: python3 foo.tar.gz, foo.zip, foo.whl; node foo.tgz, foo.tar.gz. REJECT: python3 pkg==1.0.post1, pkg==1.0.dev1.
suggested_fix: Reject names ending in .whl/.zip/.tar.gz/.tgz/.tar. Allow an optional '.' before post/dev (or parse with packaging.requirements.Requirement and require name + '==' specifier only).

title: Dependency cache key ignores interpreter/runtime version
failure_scenario: The cache path is <tool-id-hash>/<python3|node>/<requirements-hash>. It doesn't include the Python ABI (e.g. cp312) or Node major version. Caches live in the persistent omniforge_lib volume, so after an image upgrade (e.g. python:3.13-slim, or a Debian Node bump) a complete cache built for the old interpreter is reused. Packages with compiled extensions then fail at import time, and nothing triggers a reinstall.
evidence: Code inspection: digest = sha256(json.dumps(requirements)); the runtime path/version isn't part of the key and the .complete marker stores only the requirements. Not reproduced (would need two interpreter versions).
suggested_fix: Include sys.implementation.cache_tag / `python -c 'import sys;print(sys.version_info[:2])'` or `node --version` major in the digest or directory name.

title: JSON-RPC envelope errors return FastAPI 422 bodies (parsed before auth) instead of -32700/-32600
failure_scenario: Because /mcp declares `payload: dict`, FastAPI rejects malformed JSON and batch arrays with HTTP 422 {"detail":[...]} that echoes the submitted input, before _check_api_key runs. Clients get a non-JSON-RPC error they can't correlate, and unauthenticated callers get validation responses instead of 401. A message with no method or jsonrpc field returns -32601 'Method not found: None' instead of -32600 Invalid Request.
evidence: Verified. '{not json' returned 422 {"detail":[{"type":"dict_type",...,"input":"{not json"}]}. A batch [{...ping...}] returned 422. An unauthenticated '[1,2]' returned 422, not 401. {"id":3} returned {"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found: None"}}.
suggested_fix: Take the raw Request, check auth first, parse the body manually and return -32700 on parse errors and -32600 for non-object or missing method/jsonrpc. Either support batches (2025-03-26) or reject them with -32600.

title: initialize echoes any protocolVersion (even empty), ping returns null, unknown tools aren't protocol errors
failure_scenario: Version negotiation is skipped: the server agrees to whatever the client sends, including '' when the field is missing or an unsupported date, so clients believe a version is supported that the server never implemented. ping returns result:null, but MCP specifies an empty object; SDK clients that validate the result as an object (e.g. the TypeScript SDK's EmptyResultSchema) treat ping as failed. tools/call for an unknown or inactive tool returns a successful JSON-RPC result with isError, whereas the spec lists unknown tools as a -32602 protocol error.
evidence: Verified. initialize with protocolVersion '1999-01-01' returned protocolVersion '1999-01-01'. Without the field it returned protocolVersion ''. ping returned {"result":null}. tools/call does_not_exist returned result {isError:true,'Unknown or inactive tool'}.
suggested_fix: Keep a SUPPORTED_VERSIONS list and reply with the requested version if supported, else the latest supported. Return {} for ping. Return a JSON-RPC -32602 error for unknown tool names.

title: GET /mcp returns an unauthenticated SSE stream that closes immediately
failure_scenario: Streamable HTTP clients may open GET /mcp for server-initiated messages. Instead of 405 Method Not Allowed (the spec's answer when no stream is offered), they get 200 text/event-stream with a non-standard 'initial-connections' event, and the stream ends at once. Clients treat that as a dropped connection and reconnect repeatedly. The endpoint skips the API key check.
suggested_fix: Return 405 with Allow: POST (after the auth check) until a real SSE stream exists.

title: API key comparison isn't constant-time, and the raw key is accepted without the Bearer scheme
failure_scenario: token == API_KEY leaks timing information about how much of the key matched. Any Authorization header without the 'Bearer ' prefix is compared verbatim, so the key works as a bare header value; some proxies log that more readily. The 401 lacks a WWW-Authenticate header, which some MCP clients need to detect auth requirements.
evidence: Verified. 'Authorization: test-key' (no Bearer) returned 200 for ping. Code: main.py:221-222.
suggested_fix: Require the Bearer scheme, compare with hmac.compare_digest(token.encode(), API_KEY.encode()), and add WWW-Authenticate: Bearer to the 401.

title: PUT silently re-enables disabled tools and wipes their input schema when fields are omitted
failure_scenario: PUT /api/tools/{name} reuses ToolIn, which defaults is_active=True and json_schema={}. An API client or script that updates only name and code republishes a deliberately disabled tool to every MCP client. It also replaces the tool's input schema with 'no inputs', so existing callers passing arguments are now rejected. The dashboard sends both fields and isn't affected.
evidence: Verified. Tool t_dis had is_active=false and schema {type: object, properties: {x}}. A PUT with only {name, code} returned 200, after which is_active=true and the schema became {"type":"object","properties":{},"additionalProperties":false}.
suggested_fix: Use a separate update model where is_active/json_schema/description/requirements default to the existing values (check model_fields_set), or require all fields on PUT.

title: REST 422 responses echo submitted code and arguments
failure_scenario: The MCP path deliberately strips inputs from validation errors ('Do not echo submitted values, code or secrets'). The REST API uses FastAPI's default handler, which returns the full submitted value in detail[].input. Scripts and test arguments that contain credentials end up in error bodies, browser devtools/HAR captures and any reverse-proxy or APM logging of error responses.
evidence: Verified. POST /api/tools with a code value containing NUL returned 422 with "input":"print('synthetic-echo-check')\u0000". POST /run with arguments ["synthetic-arg-echo"] returned 422 echoing the array.
suggested_fix: Register a RequestValidationError handler that returns only loc and msg (as call_tool does with include_input=False).

title: MCP tools/call executes from the 5-second process cache while dashboard runs read fresh rows
failure_scenario: call_tool resolves the tool from db.get_tool_list(), which is cached for OMNIFORGE_CACHE_TTL_MS, while api_run_tool uses get_tool(fresh=True). With more than one uvicorn worker, or after any out-of-process DB change, MCP clients can run the previous code or a just-disabled tool for up to 5 s while the dashboard shows the new state. api_update_tool also reads `existing` from the cache, and a PUT without If-Match can re-insert (resurrect) a tool another worker just deleted, via ON CONFLICT(id).
evidence: Verified. After priming the cache, the code was changed directly in SQLite (simulating another worker). MCP tools/call returned 'version 1' immediately afterwards, while POST /api/tools/t_ver/run returned 'version 2'.
suggested_fix: Fetch the single row fresh (SELECT by name, active) in tools/call, or invalidate the cache on PRAGMA data_version changes. In api_update_tool, use get_tool(fresh=True) and fail the upsert if the id no longer exists.

title: No size limits on code, description, schema or request bodies
failure_scenario: ToolIn and CREATE_SCHEMA set no maxLength on description, code or inputSchema, and the app sets no body-size limit. A tool with a multi-megabyte description (e.g. created by an LLM through omniforge_create_tool) is sent in every tools/list to every client, overflowing LLM context windows and breaking all chats that load the server. GET /api/tools also returns every tool's full code on each dashboard load.
evidence: Code inspection: tool_authoring.py:76-81 and mcp_server.py:16-30 have no length bounds; main.py has no body-size middleware. Large stdout passing through untruncated (BE-09) shows the same absence of caps. Not separately reproduced with a large description.
suggested_fix: Add maxLength (e.g. description 2 KB, code 256 KB, schema 64 KB) to ToolIn and CREATE_SCHEMA, and a request-size limit in front of the app.

title: Unpinned and undeclared dependencies, an untested :latest publish, and compose/image drift
failure_scenario: app/tool_authoring.py imports jsonschema and referencing directly, but they aren't in requirements.txt; they arrive only because the otherwise unused `mcp` package requires jsonschema>=4.20. All requirements are unpinned, and dockerhub.yml builds and pushes dbzocchi/omniforge:latest on every main push without running tests (test.yml excludes main). A new upstream release (an mcp release dropping jsonschema, or a FastAPI/Starlette/pydantic behaviour change) can produce a broken image that is published as latest. There is also drift: docker-compose.yml names the image ionic-developer/omniforge:latest (not the pushed dbzocchi/omniforge), sets unused OMNIFORGE_RUNTIME_IMAGE and an unused scripts volume while scratch defaults to /tmp/omniforge, and there is no health endpoint or HEALTHCHECK.
evidence: requirements.txt lists fastapi, uvicorn[standard], pydantic, pydantic-settings, mcp, sse-starlette, slowapi, all unpinned. importlib.metadata shows jsonschema 4.26.0 / referencing 0.37.0 present only via mcp 2.3.0 ('jsonschema>=4.20.0'). No app module imports mcp, sse_starlette, slowapi or pydantic_settings. dockerhub.yml has no test step.
suggested_fix: Declare jsonschema and referencing explicitly, drop unused packages, pin via a lock/constraints file, run the unittest suite in the publish workflow before pushing, align the compose image name, and remove dead env/volumes. Add a /healthz endpoint and Docker HEALTHCHECK.
